pages.text: A core of mass M has a Schwarzschild radius r_s = 2GM/c². Held at r from it, a sample's clock runs slower than the world's by 1/√(1 − r_s/r). The work the chamber does in its own time is that many times more, measured outside.
$(thing)Set$(): Core mass, Sample distance.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The core's mass flickers by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The samples have fallen through the horizon.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): More dilation, and a bigger chamber, do more.
